newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe deflation at 0.15 pct in Nov 16-Dec 15.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe deflation at 0.15 pct in Nov 16-Dec 15.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) fell 0.15 percent between November 16 and December 15, said a Fipe official.
Prices fell in the period, compared with a 0.03 percent deflation in the prior four-week period, due mostly to a drop in food prices, said Juarez Rizzieri, president of the Fipe Institute.

Rizzieri said he expects December will end with close to zero inflation, against November's 0.34 percent rise, despite a slight impact of the recently announced increase in fuel prices on the Fipe index.
He estimates that the hike in fuel prices will have an impact of 0.2 percent in December's inflation, considering increases in gasoline prices between 10 percent and 12 percent on average.
For the whole of 1996, Rizzieri expects inflation at around 10 percent.
Rizzieri also announced the following breakdown of its weighted inflation index for the period:
- Food -1.15 pct drop in the period
- Housing 0.46 pct rise in the period
- Transportation -0.07 pct drop in the period
- Personal expenses 0.04 pct rise in the period
- Clothing 0.36 pct rise in the period
- Health care 0.81 pct rise in the period
- Education 0.53 pct rise in the period
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures at weekly intervals.
